SK Advanced Co Ltd Announces Major Expansion to Boost Propylene Output

SK Advanced Co Ltd, a leading player in South Korea’s chemicals industry, has unveiled plans for a significant expansion of its propylene production capacity in Ulsan, responding to robust demand from both domestic and international markets.

The company announced on Tuesday that it will invest approximately KRW 370 billion (about USD 270 million) in the construction of a new production line adjacent to its existing facilities. Once completed by late 2026, the expansion is expected to increase SK Advanced’s annual propylene output by 200,000 metric tons, bringing its total capacity to 800,000 metric tons per year.

“The global chemicals market is undergoing rapid transformation, with demand for high-purity propylene continuing to outpace supply,” said Choi Min-seok, Chief Executive Officer of SK Advanced Co Ltd. “With this investment, we are reinforcing our position as a key supplier for industries ranging from packaging and automotive parts to medical equipment.”

Analysts note that the move comes as regional manufacturers seek to secure stable supplies of essential feedstocks amid ongoing volatility in global supply chains. “SK Advanced’s expansion signals confidence in the resilience of Korea’s chemical sector and its ability to capture new business from Southeast Asia and beyond,” said Lee Hyun-woo, a chemicals analyst at Seoul-based market research firm Hanil Insight.

Local authorities welcomed the announcement, citing the project’s potential to create new jobs and stimulate the regional economy. “This investment will have a direct impact on Ulsan by generating up to 250 new jobs during the construction phase and supporting long-term employment in operations and maintenance,” said Park Ji-hyun, Deputy Mayor of Ulsan Metropolitan City. “SK Advanced has been a valued corporate citizen, and we look forward to supporting their continued growth.”

The Korea Petrochemical Industry Association also issued a statement backing the project, describing it as “an important step towards securing the competitiveness of Korea’s value-added chemical products on the global stage.”

SK Advanced Co Ltd was established in 2014 and operates one of the country’s largest propane dehydrogenation (PDH) plants, utilizing advanced process technology to produce high-purity propylene for downstream sectors.

Construction on the new production line is slated to begin in the third quarter of this year, with SK Advanced targeting commercial operations by December 2026. Company officials said that the expanded facility will incorporate new energy efficiency measures and emissions controls in line with Korea’s Green New Deal targets.

Shares of SK Advanced were up 2.1% on Tuesday following the announcement.
